reason: CONFIRMED by driving and by sampling painted pixels, not computed values. Code: shell.css:314 is the single ring rule (outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px); b.css:30 sets :root --focus: var(--fore) and b.css:31 sets [data-ground=paper] --focus: var(--accent); shell.css:156-171 makes --fore = --paper (#fff) on ink. b.css:1056 gives .b-chat background: var(--paper) and b.css:1073-1080 gives .b-unfurl background: var(--paper), both literal, both grounds - the plate is hard white in the ink room too. Driven at file://.../master.html?v=<ground>&state=<state>, chromium, deviceScaleFactor 1, tabbing with real Tab presses. On ?v=ink, .b-unfurl focuses (matches(':focus-visible') true) with outlineColor rgb(255,255,255) on a chatBg of rgb(255,255,255): 1.00:1. Pixel strips across the ring band on ALL FOUR sides at 1..8px outside the border box read 255,255,255 at every distance, in publish and in unfurl, at 1440x960 and 390x844 - identical to the same strips with the element blurred. The strongest measurement: a whole-viewport diff of the focused vs unfocused screenshot on ink changes ZERO pixels in all four ink cases, while the same diff on paper changes ~2200 pixels (first differing pixel [255,255,255] -> [199,197,247], the antialiased edge of the indigo ring). So no shift, no shadow, no border change, no inner ring - box-shadow computes 'none', transform 'none', borderTopColor rgba(17,17,17,0.16) focused and blurred alike. There is literally no visible focus affordance on ink. Paper is the control: same element, outlineColor rgb(79,70,229), indigo measured in the band at +3 and +4px on top, bottom, left and right, 6.29:1 against the white plate, and it disappears on blur. The severity claim holds: the full tab ring on state=unfurl is [A.b-unfurl, (body)] - .b-unfurl is the ONLY focusable element on that screen, so an ink-room keyboard user has no indicator anywhere; on publish it is stop 2 (b-act, b-unfurl, b-linkField, b-act). The token really is unscoped: .b-chat carries no --focus of its own, and the only focusable inside .b-chat in any state is .b-unfurl (checked across all fourteen states; .b-chat renders only on publish and unfurl). Neither gate can see it: interaction-check.mjs:109-118 grabs document.querySelector('button, a[href], [tabindex], input') - one element - and returns true on parseFloat(outlineWidth) > 0, colour-blind by construction; audit.mjs treats outlineColor only as a palette-lock prop (line 189/194) - white is on palette - and its contrast pass (lines 340-365, 230-245) is text-only, keyed on size/weight/text, and runs with nothing focused. This is the round-10 class recurring on a different token, and it is not in SETTLED.md.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix as proposed, one line beside the .b-chat block in b.css (after b.css:1056): `.b-chat { --focus: var(--accent); }`. Verified by injecting exactly that rule at runtime and re-measuring both grounds, both states, 1440x960 and 390x844: on ink .b-unfurl's ring becomes rgb(79,70,229) and paints indigo at +3px on all four sides against the [255,255,255] plate (6.29:1); the focused-vs-unfocused viewport diff goes from 0 changed pixels to ~2200, matching paper exactly. Paper is byte-for-byte unchanged. Nothing else moves: .b-unfurl is the only focusable descendant of .b-chat in any state, and every control outside the plate keeps its own ground's ring (ink: .b-act and .b-linkField still rgb(255,255,255); paper: still rgb(79,70,229)). Scope it on .b-chat rather than .b-unfurl so the rest of the plate - bubble, any future control on somebody else's light surface - inherits the same correction. Two things worth doing in the same stroke, both cheap: (1) b.css:31's comment should say the rule is 'ring follows the LOCAL ground, not the room's', since .b-chat is the second ground on this page; (2) interaction-check.mjs:109-118 should sample the composited backdrop under the ring and assert a ratio rather than outlineWidth > 0, or this class returns on the next literal-white island. Neither is required for the fix to land.
